hsk30idm/一窍不通.why: The idiom's gloss carried its literal sense inline, marked `lit.`, so the picture that makes the idiom memorable was buried in the middle of a run-on definition. Split: the meaning stays in the gloss and the image moves to the Literally line the card type now renders under it.  ALSO: The note had fewer than the three example sentences the card type shows and the decks' own bank had nothing usable left for it. These come from the TATOEBA corpus (CC BY 2.0 FR), which is where the decks' existing sentences come from — 60% of them are verbatim in Tatoeba's own Mandarin-English pairs — so this is the same source rather than a new one. Filters: the sentence must contain the headword and NOT have it swallowed by a longer headword in the same place, must carry no traditional-only character (the decks are simplified, and the corpus is mixed), no Latin letters, 36 characters at most, and a translation not already on the card. No structure line: it cannot be derived for a sentence written for a different headword.

hintsWhy: AUTHORITATIVE: this map is the complete list of `not X` blocks in the Mandarin decks, including the 104 pairs the generator itself produced — it is regenerated from the finished decks, so a pair that stops colliding loses its block rather than keeping one that points at nothing. The English → Chinese card's front is the gloss and nothing else, so two notes sharing one are a question with two right answers. These are the 251 PAIRS that had no disambiguator; each member is given the deck's own `not <other word>` block, the shape 104 pairs already carry. A group of three or more is not hinted — naming four of five answers on the front is worse than the ambiguity — and is given a distinguishing gloss in `notes` instead.

decks.why: A learner met nine decks presented as nine levels with nothing to say where to start, how big each was against the others, or where the two decks outside the ladder fit. The Collections page prints this line under the deck's title. It replaces a subtitle that restated the word count and the direction, both of which the row already shows for itself.

addFields.name: Literally

decks.whyFields: An idiom's gloss says what it MEANS and throws away what it SAYS, which is the picture that makes a four-character idiom memorable: 谢天谢地 is 'thank goodness' and it says 'thank heaven, thank earth'. The Literally line is added to the Chinese → English card, under the meaning.
decks.whyCredit: The decks' example sentences come from Tatoeba and carried no attribution — 60% of the 20,010 shipped sentences are verbatim in Tatoeba's own Mandarin-English pairs, and Tatoeba is CC BY 2.0 FR, which requires credit. Added to every deck's description, which is what the Collections page and the Studio show.
